details:
The built-in Eye Look feature for the VRC Avatar Descriptor is a great feature for all of the users that do not have or cannot afford eye-tracking features for their avatars, and I think it would be really cool for that to be expanded upon so that more customization is available in regards to avatar creation techniques.

In the same way that Visemes have Built-in Animator Parameters (the integer value that infers which viseme the player is triggering with their voice, that we can use to trigger certain states in an Animator), I think a lot of users would find much use in a similar set of parameters for the Eye Look feature.

For example, if I created an avatar that has the Eye Look feature turned on, regardless of whether or not the rig includes eye bones to support it, I could read values such as the X and Y values(-1 to 1 along both X and Y) of where the eyes are intended to be turned to, as well as how closed the eyelids are ( 0 to 1 ) and use conditions in the Animator transitions to infer how to change states based on that info.

The avatar I am currently making uses the Visemes integers to change between mouth shapes instantaneously, because I am using textured planes for a 2D "drawn-on" appearance. If the SDK included similar values, presumably floats, for the current conditions of eyes, I'd be able to have easier control over how to switch states for my avatar's eyes, which are configured to use the same method as the mouth.
title: Built-In Animator Parameters for Eyes
